chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from someone who heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

When al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) was near death, he wept, so it was said to him: 'O son of the daughter of Allah's Messenger, you are weeping despite your position with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) being the one you are in, and despite the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) having said about you what he said, and despite your having performed pilgrimage twenty times riding and twenty times on foot, and despite having given away your wealth to your Lord three times, even down to your sandals?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'I only weep for two things: the terror of what is to come and separation from loved ones.'

key_terms.هول المطلع: The terror/awe of what is to come (the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir weep at the time of death despite his high status and piety?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the emotional response to death is distinguished from mere fear of punishment, highlighting the dual spiritual burdens of the 'awe of the Ascension' (Hawl al-Multaq) and the 'sorrow of parting from loved ones' (Firaq al-Ahbab). This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's household as the ultimate spiritual companions, making their separation a profound existential grief even for the Imams. The context underscores that true piety involves balancing confidence in divine mercy with humility before the majesty of the Hereafter.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 6.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from someone who heard Abā Jaʿfar (a) say,

“When al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (a) was on his deathbed, he cried, so someone asked him, ‘O son of the daughter of Allah’s Messenger, you are crying despite having the position that you have next to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ)? And despite what the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) has said regarding you? And despite your having gone for pilgrimage twenty times riding and twenty times on foot? And despite having given away all your possessions for the sake of Allah thrice, even your sandals?’ He (a) replied, ‘I am only weeping for two things: the terror of what is to come [in the grave and Hereafter] and separation from loved ones.’”
